questions.p: Chamber of commerce na body wey dey push trade, settle wahala, organise trade fair and talk for business people front of government; e no be manufacturer, na the member companies dey make and sell their own goods.

questions.q: A major function of the Consumer Protection Council (or similar consumer protection agency) in Nigeria is to:
o: Investigate complaints from consumers against poor quality or harmful goods
Grant soft loans to small-scale traders
Fix minimum wage for workers in private companies
Issue import licences to foreign companies
questions.e: Consumer protection agencies exist mainly to safeguard the interest of buyers by receiving and investigating complaints about substandard, unsafe or harmful goods and services sold to the public.
questions.p: Consumer protection agency work na to protect the buyer, so dem dey receive and investigate complain wey consumers bring about bad quality or harmful goods wey dem buy.

questions.q: One major advantage a small trader, Mama Ngozi, enjoys by joining her local traders' association is that the association can:
o: Provide free transportation of her goods across states
Automatically exempt her from paying company income tax
Guarantee her a direct government supply contract
Give members collective bargaining power to get better terms from suppliers
questions.e: Trade associations negotiate on behalf of many small traders at once, so members often get better prices, credit terms or discounts from suppliers than they could get bargaining alone.
questions.p: Trade association dey yarn with suppliers for behalf of plenty traders together, so members fit get better price, credit or discount pass if na them one go bargain alone.

questions.q: Some soap manufacturers in Aba form a trade association and then secretly agree among themselves to fix a high common price and limit the quantity of soap each member produces. This action would most likely lead to:
o: Exploitation of consumers through higher prices and reduced choice
A reduction in soap prices due to healthy competition
Automatic increase in the quality of soap produced
Improved bargaining power for consumers over the manufacturers
questions.e: When members of a trade association collude to fix prices and restrict output, they behave like a cartel, which harms consumers by raising prices and limiting the amount and variety of goods available; this is exactly the kind of practice consumer protection bodies try to prevent.
questions.p: If the soap makers come join hand fix high price and limit how much soap dem go produce, na cartel behaviour be that, and e go make price go up and consumer go get less choice, that na why consumer protection body dey fight this kain gragra.

questions.q: The key difference between a trade association and a trade union is that:
o: Trade association fixes workers' wages while trade union fixes consumer prices
Trade association represents consumers while trade union represents employers
Trade association is for employers or firms in the same trade while trade union is for workers or employees
Trade association and trade union are formed only by the government
questions.e: A trade association is made up of business owners or firms in the same line of trade protecting business interests, while a trade union is made up of employees who join together to protect workers' welfare and bargain with employers over wages and conditions.
questions.p: Trade association na for business owners or company wey dey do same trade, dem dey protect business interest; trade union na for workers wey join hand protect their welfare and bargain with employer for wages and condition of service.

questions.q: Which of the following is recognised as a basic right of consumers that consumer protection laws seek to guarantee?
o: The right to personally fix the selling price of goods bought in a shop
The right to safety from goods that are hazardous to health
The right to stop other consumers from buying certain goods
The right to manufacture competing products freely without registration
questions.e: One of the basic rights of a consumer is the right to safety, meaning they should be protected from goods and services that could harm their health or life, such as expired drugs or unsafe electrical appliances.
questions.p: One of the basic right wey consumer get na right to safety, meaning say make dem no suffer from goods wey fit harm their body, like expired medicine or bad electrical gadget.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic functions of management as identified by classical management theorists such as Henri Fayol?
questions.e: Fayol's classical functions of management are planning, organising, commanding/directing, coordinating and controlling. Marketing is a specific business function (like production or finance), not a general management function.
questions.p: Fayol im management functions na planning, organising, directing, coordinating and controlling. Marketing na business function wey dey under one department, e no be general management function.

questions.q: In a typical business organisation, the level of management that is directly responsible for the day-to-day supervision of workers on the factory floor is called the:
questions.e: Lower or supervisory management works closest to the workers and handles daily, routine supervision of operations. Top management sets overall policy, while middle management coordinates between the two levels.
questions.p: Lower or supervisory management na dem dey close to di workers, dem dey handle daily, normal supervision of work. Top management na dem dey set big policy, middle management dey connect top and lower level.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze, the Managing Director of a Lagos-based bakery, has the Production Manager, Sales Manager and Finance Manager reporting directly to her. The number of people who report directly to Mrs Adaeze is referred to as her:
questions.e: Span of control is the number of subordinates that a manager directly supervises. Here, Mrs Adaeze directly supervises three managers, so her span of control is 3.
questions.p: Span of control na di number of people wey dey report directly to one manager. Mrs Adaeze get three managers wey dey report to am, so her span of control na three.

questions.q: A company structures its staff into separate departments such as Production, Marketing, Finance and Human Resources, with each department head being an expert in that specific area. This type of organisational structure is called:
questions.e: Functional organisation groups workers according to the specialised activity or function they perform, such as marketing or finance. This allows specialists to head each department based on their expertise.
questions.p: Functional organisation na when dem group workers based on di specific work wey dem dey do, like marketing or finance. Na why specialist dey head each department.

questions.q: The management principle which states that each employee should receive orders from only one superior at a time is known as the principle of:
questions.e: Unity of command means every worker should take instructions from one boss only, to avoid confusion and conflicting orders. This principle was strongly emphasised by Henri Fayol.
questions.p: Unity of command mean say each worker suppose dey take order from just one boss, so dat confusion no go dey. Na Fayol talk am well well.

questions.q: A trading company reorganised its staff so that the Marketing Manager gives marketing instructions to workers in every department, while the Production Manager gives production instructions to the same workers. Soon, many workers began receiving conflicting orders from both managers on the same day. This confusion is a common weakness of which type of organisational structure?
questions.e: In functional organisation, specialist managers give orders across departments based on their area of expertise, which can break the principle of unity of command and cause conflicting instructions to the same workers. This is a well-known drawback of pure functional structures compared to line organisation.
questions.p: For functional organisation, different specialist managers dey give order for different departments based on their area, so dem fit break unity of command and workers go dey confuse with different order. Na common wahala for functional structure pass line organisation.

questions.q: Delegation of authority in an organisation best means that a manager:
o: Gives up all control and responsibility over a department forever
Employs new staff to replace an underperforming worker
Permanently transfers ownership of the business to a subordinate
Gives a subordinate the right to take certain decisions within set limits, while the manager remains ultimately responsible
questions.e: Delegation means a manager passes down specific authority to a subordinate to make decisions within agreed limits, but the manager still carries final responsibility for the outcome. It does not mean giving away ownership or permanent control.
questions.p: Delegation mean say manager go give subordinate small power make e fit take some decision within di limit wey dem agree, but di manager still carry final responsibility. E no mean say manager don give away ownership forever.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's transport company has 1 General Manager who directly supervises 3 Branch Managers. Each of the 3 Branch Managers directly supervises 6 drivers. What is the total number of people in the company, including the General Manager?
questions.e: Total = General Manager + Branch Managers + Drivers = 1 + 3 + (3 x 6) = 1 + 3 + 18 = 22. Counting every level of the organisation gives 22 people in total.
questions.p: Total = General Manager + Branch Managers + Drivers = 1 + 3 + (3 x 6) = 1 + 3 + 18 = 22. If you count everybody for di organisation structure, you go reach 22 people.

questions.q: What is the main focus of the modern marketing concept as practised by businesses in Nigeria?
o: Producing goods as cheaply as possible
Satisfying customer needs and wants profitably
Increasing the number of advertisements only
questions.e: The marketing concept puts the customer first, aiming to identify and satisfy their needs while still making profit for the business. It is different from just focusing on production or pushing sales.
questions.p: Marketing concept mean say business go first find out wetin customer want, then satisfy am make profit still enter. E no be just to produce cheap or push sell-sell.

questions.q: The marketing mix is often summarised as the '4Ps'. Which of the following is NOT one of the 4Ps?
questions.e: The 4Ps of marketing are Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Profit is a business goal but it is not one of the 4Ps elements of the marketing mix.
questions.p: The 4Ps na Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Profit na result wey business dey find, but e no be part of the 4Ps.

questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix is concerned with the channels used to move goods from the producer to the final consumer?
questions.e: Place deals with distribution, that is, how goods move from the producer, through middlemen like wholesalers and retailers, to reach the final consumer. Product is about the item itself, while Price and Promotion are different elements.
questions.p: Place na the one wey dey handle how goods dey waka comot from producer reach the final consumer, through wholesalers and retailers. Product na about the item, Price na cost, Promotion na how dem advertise am.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Aba reduces the cost of his chairs during the Christmas season so that more customers can afford to buy. This decision mainly concerns which element of the marketing mix?
questions.e: Reducing the amount customers pay for the chairs is a pricing decision, since price refers to the amount charged for a product. It is not about changing the product itself, its distribution, or its advertisement.
questions.p: To reduce how much customer go pay na Price decision, because Price na the amount wey dem dey charge for product. E no be about the chair design, how e dey reach market, or advert.

questions.q: Which of the following activities by a soft drink company best illustrates the 'promotion' element of the marketing mix?
o: Running a radio jingle to inform customers about the drink
Designing a new bottle shape for the drink
Building a warehouse closer to retailers in Kano
questions.e: Promotion involves communicating with customers to inform, persuade or remind them about a product, and a radio jingle is a clear example of this. The other options relate to product design, place/distribution, and price respectively.
questions.p: Promotion na when business dey inform or persuade customer about product, and radio jingle na clear example of that. The other options dey talk about product design, distribution (place), and price.

questions.q: Chioma, an entrepreneur, first studies what her customers want before producing her organic honey, then designs the product, price, packaging and distribution to satisfy those needs while still making profit. This approach best illustrates the:
questions.e: Chioma starts from customer needs before producing and arranging the full marketing mix, which is the essence of the marketing concept. The selling and production concepts focus more on pushing output or sales rather than starting from customer needs.
questions.p: Chioma first check wetin customers want before she produce and arrange product, price, packaging and distribution, na so marketing concept take be. Selling and production concepts dey focus on pushing output or sales instead of customer need first.

questions.q: A company believes that as long as it produces goods cheaply and makes them widely available, customers will automatically buy, without studying their specific needs. This belief reflects the:
questions.e: The production concept assumes that customers mainly want cheap, widely available products, so the business focuses on efficiency and mass production rather than studying actual customer needs. This is different from the marketing concept, which starts with understanding the customer.
questions.p: Production concept na when business believe say if goods cheap and dey everywhere, customers go just buy, without the business first check wetin customer really want. E different from marketing concept wey dey start from understanding customer.

questions.q: For a bottled water company, which of the following best represents the 'product' element of its marketing mix?
o: The amount charged per bottle at retail outlets
The billboard adverts used to create awareness of the water
The actual bottle of water, including its branding, size and quality
The route trucks use to deliver water to shops in Lagos
questions.e: Product refers to the actual good or service offered, including its features such as branding, size and quality, which satisfies the customer's need. The delivery route is 'place', the amount charged is 'price', and the billboard is 'promotion'.
questions.p: Product na the actual item wey dem dey sell, with im branding, size and quality, wey dey satisfy customer need. The delivery route na 'place', the amount na 'price', and the billboard na 'promotion'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as an essential element required for a valid contract?
o: An implied warranty attached to goods sold
Offer and acceptance by the parties
Legal capacity of the parties to contract
questions.e: A valid contract needs offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity and intention to create legal relations. An implied warranty is a term that may apply in sale of goods, not a general requirement for forming any contract.
questions.p: For contract to dey valid, e need offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity and intention. Implied warranty na something wey dey apply for sale of goods matter, e no be general rule for all contract.

questions.q: In the law of contract, what does 'consideration' mean?
o: The price written on the receipt of a transaction
The written document used to record an agreement
Something of value given by one party in return for a promise made by the other
The person who witnesses the signing of an agreement
questions.e: Consideration is the value (money, goods, service or a promise) that each party gives in exchange for the other party's promise. Without consideration, most simple contracts cannot be enforced.
questions.p: Consideration na the value wey one party give in exchange for the promise wey the other party give. If no consideration, the ordinary contract no fit stand for court.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze appoints Tunde to sell her goods and agrees to pay him extra commission if he personally guarantees that buyers will pay for the goods they collect on credit. What type of agent is Tunde in this arrangement?
o: A del credere agent, because he guarantees payment to the principal for extra pay
A sub-agent appointed by another agent
questions.e: A del credere agent receives extra commission for guaranteeing that customers he sells to on credit will pay. This is different from a general or universal agent, who simply has wide or unlimited powers without such a guarantee.
questions.p: Del credere agent na agent wey dey collect extra commission because e dey guarantee say the customer go pay the money wey e owe. Na different thing from universal agent wey just get wide power to act.

questions.q: Under the Sale of Goods Law, when goods are sold by description (for example, 'a bag of 50kg rice, Mama Gold brand'), there is an implied condition that the goods delivered must:
o: be of merchantable quality only, regardless of description
be free from any charge or encumbrance in favour of a third party
be fit for the buyer's particular purpose only
correspond with the description given at the time of sale
questions.e: When goods are sold by description, the law implies a condition that the actual goods delivered must match that description. If a trader delivers a different brand or weight from what was described, the buyer can reject the goods.
questions.p: When dem sell goods with description, na condition say the goods wey dem bring must match the description. If the trader bring different brand or weight, buyer fit reject am.

questions.q: Chidi bought a generator on hire purchase from Emeka Stores and had paid only part of the instalments. Before completing payment, Chidi sold the generator to Ngozi, who bought it in good faith believing Chidi was the owner. Under hire purchase law, who has the better title to the generator?
o: Nobody has title; the generator automatically becomes abandoned property
Emeka Stores, because ownership of goods under hire purchase remains with the seller until the final instalment is paid
Chidi, because he was in physical possession of the generator
Ngozi, because she bought in good faith and did not know about the agreement
questions.e: Under hire purchase, the hirer (Chidi) only has possession, not ownership, until all instalments are paid. Since he had no ownership, he could not transfer a better title than he had (nemo dat quod non habet), so Emeka Stores remains the rightful owner.
questions.p: For hire purchase, the person wey dey pay installment (Chidi) no be owner until e finish pay everything, na only possession e get. Since e no be owner, e no fit sell wetin e no get, so Emeka Stores still remain the real owner.

questions.q: Which of the following types of contract must generally be evidenced in writing before it can be enforced in court?
o: An oral agreement to repair a bicycle for ₦500
A contract of guarantee, where one person promises to pay another's debt if that person defaults
A verbal agreement to supply firewood to a neighbour
A contract for the sale of a bag of rice at the market
questions.e: Contracts of guarantee are special contracts that the law requires to be evidenced in writing (in line with the Statute of Frauds principle) before they can be enforced, unlike most simple everyday contracts which can be oral.
questions.p: Contract of guarantee na special one wey law say must dey written down before court go enforce am, unlike ordinary everyday contract wey fit dey verbal.

questions.q: Musa, a 16-year-old secondary school student, enters into a contract to buy a motorcycle (not a necessary item for him) on credit. Under the general law of contract, what is the status of this contract as regards Musa?
o: It is void and unenforceable against Musa, as he lacks capacity for non-necessary contracts
It is valid and fully enforceable against Musa like any adult's contract
It is binding on Musa's parents alone, since he is still a minor
It becomes valid automatically once Musa turns 25 years old
questions.e: A minor generally lacks full legal capacity to contract. Except for contracts for necessaries or beneficial contracts of service, agreements made by a minor for non-necessary items are void and cannot be enforced against the minor.
questions.p: Minor no get full capacity to enter contract. Apart from necessaries or beneficial service contract, any contract wey minor enter for non-necessary thing no valid and court no go enforce am against am.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the doctrine of 'caveat emptor' as applied in the law of sale of goods?
o: The buyer has no right to reject goods, however defective they may be
The buyer is automatically protected by an unlimited seller's warranty
The buyer must examine goods carefully before buying, since the seller is not generally liable for defects the buyer ought to have discovered
The seller must refund the buyer at any time the buyer is dissatisfied
questions.e: Caveat emptor means 'let the buyer beware'. It places the responsibility on the buyer to check goods carefully before purchase, as the seller is not automatically liable for obvious defects, except where implied conditions under the Sale of Goods Law are broken.
questions.p: Caveat emptor mean say 'make buyer dey careful'. E mean say na buyer responsibility to check the goods well before e buy, because seller no dey automatically liable for defect wey buyer suppose don see, except where the law implied conditions apply.

questions.q: What is the best definition of e-commerce as used in business studies?
o: The advertisement of goods and services on radio stations
The transportation of goods from one town to another by road
The use of a computer only to type business letters
The buying and selling of goods and services electronically, usually over the internet
questions.e: E-commerce simply means carrying out trade activities such as buying, selling and payment using electronic means like the internet. The other options describe ordinary business or transport activities that are not necessarily electronic trade.
questions.p: E-commerce na when people dey buy and sell goods or services through electronic means like internet. The other options na just normal business work wey no concern electronic trade.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct example of Business-to-Consumer (B2C) e-commerce?
o: A government ministry paying a road contractor electronically for a completed project
Jumia selling a phone directly to Ade, who is the final user of the phone
Dangote Cement supplying many bags of cement to a registered cement distributor company
Chioma selling her used wrapper to Ngozi through a social media group
questions.e: B2C means a registered business sells directly to the final consumer, as Jumia does to Ade. The other options show business-to-business, consumer-to-consumer and government-to-business transactions respectively.
questions.p: B2C na when real business dey sell straight to the person wey go use the product, like Jumia and Ade. The other examples na business-to-business, consumer-to-consumer and government-to-business.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of e-commerce to a trader?
o: It removes the need for the trader to advertise his goods
It guarantees that every customer will pay cash before the goods are delivered
It allows the trader's business to reach customers far beyond his locality at any time of the day
It removes the need for the trader to have internet access
questions.e: A major benefit of e-commerce is wider market reach, since customers anywhere can view and order goods online at any time. E-commerce actually needs internet access, cannot guarantee payment behaviour, and advertising is still important for visibility.
questions.p: Big advantage of e-commerce na say customer wey dey far from you fit still buy your goods anytime because of internet. E-commerce no fit work without internet, e no guarantee say person go pay cash, and advert still dey important.

questions.q: In e-commerce, the electronic exchange of structured business documents such as invoices and purchase orders directly between the computers of two trading partners is known as?
questions.e: EDI specifically refers to computer-to-computer exchange of standard business documents like invoices and orders between companies. ATM, POS and EFT are related to payments and cash withdrawal, not document exchange.
questions.p: EDI na when computer dey send business paper like invoice and order go another company computer direct. ATM, POS and EFT na more about money payment, no be document exchange.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common challenge facing the growth of e-commerce in many parts of Nigeria?
o: Unreliable electricity supply and low internet access in some areas
An excess number of skilled information technology workers
Strict government control fixing the prices of all online goods
Too many commercial banks offering online payment services
questions.e: Poor power supply and limited internet coverage in some areas make it hard for both traders and customers to use e-commerce platforms steadily. Having many banks or IT workers would actually help e-commerce, and price control is not a standard Nigerian e-commerce problem.
questions.p: Light wahala and small internet for some areas na real problem for e-commerce for Nigeria. If plenty banks or IT people dey, e for even help business; government no dey fix price for everything wey dem dey sell online.

questions.q: Mr. Eze, a wholesaler, uses a computer software that automatically updates his stock records whenever goods are sold or newly received, and alerts him when it is time to reorder. This particular use of the computer in his business is best described as?
questions.e: Tracking stock levels, updating records after sales or purchases, and signalling reorder points is exactly what inventory or stock control software does. It is not marketing, payment processing or research, since no advertising, money transfer or data survey is described.
questions.p: Wetin Mr Eze dey do na inventory control, because e dey track how much stock dey remain and e dey tell am when to order new goods. E no be marketing, payment or research, since no advert, money transfer or survey dey happen here.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best distinguishes Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce from Business-to-Consumer (B2C) e-commerce?
o: C2C involves only government agencies, while B2C involves only private companies
C2C transactions never require the internet, while B2C transactions always require the internet
C2C involves transactions directly between individual consumers, while B2C involves a registered business selling to a consumer
C2C transactions can only happen offline, while B2C transactions can only happen online
questions.e: The key difference is who the seller is: in C2C it is an ordinary individual selling to another individual, while in B2C it is a formal business selling to a consumer. The other statements wrongly limit both models to offline/online only or to government/private ownership.
questions.p: The main difference na who dey sell: for C2C na ordinary person dey sell to another person, but for B2C na real business dey sell to consumer. The other options dey wrongly limit am to offline/online or government/private only.

questions.q: Tunde wants to set up a shop that sells shoes to customers all over Nigeria through the internet and allows them to pay instantly with their bank cards. Which combination of tools would he MOST need to achieve this using e-commerce?
o: A radio jingle advertising his shop and a manual cash register at his single shop
A fax machine for orders and a postal address for customers to send letters
A printed catalogue of shoes and a local town crier announcing his prices
A company website with a shopping cart feature and a secure online payment gateway
questions.e: True e-commerce selling nationwide with instant card payment requires an online website where customers can select items (shopping cart) and pay securely online (payment gateway). Radio jingles, town criers, printed catalogues and fax machines are traditional tools that do not provide real-time online ordering and card payment.
questions.p: To really sell online well-well and collect card payment sharp-sharp, Tunde need website wit shopping cart and secure online payment gateway. Radio jingle, town crier, catalogue and fax machine na old style wey no fit give instant online order and card payment.

questions.q: Which term refers to the sum total of all internal and external factors—such as customers, government policy, culture, and competitors—that affect how a business organization operates and achieves its goals?
questions.e: The business environment is the combination of all internal and external forces that surround and influence a firm's operations. It includes things like customers, suppliers, laws, technology, and competitors.
questions.p: Business environment na all di inside and outside things wey dey affect how company dey operate, like customer, law, and competitor. E no be business cycle, policy or ethics.

questions.q: Which of the following is best classified as an INTERNAL business environment factor, rather than an external one?
questions.e: Organizational culture is created and controlled from within the business itself, unlike taxes, exchange rates, and competitor pricing which come from outside forces the firm cannot directly control.
questions.p: Organizational culture na something wey dey inside di company, so na internal factor. Tax policy, exchange rate and competitor price na external things wey dey come from outside.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's furniture workshop in Aba had to spend extra money installing waste-treatment equipment after the state government passed a new environmental sanitation law. This situation shows the influence of which business environment factor?
questions.e: A government law forcing businesses to meet certain standards is a legal factor, because it comes from government legislation that firms must obey, affecting how they operate.
questions.p: Na government law force am to buy waste equipment, so na legal factor dey affect am, because law na government rule wey business must obey.

questions.q: Business ethics in commerce is best described as
o: methods used by firms to advertise and promote products
strategies for maximizing profit regardless of method
government laws regulating the import and export of goods
rules and principles guiding fair and moral conduct in business dealings
questions.e: Business ethics deals with moral standards and fairness in how a business treats its workers, customers, and the public, not just profit-making or advertising methods.
questions.p: Business ethics na di moral rules wey dey guide how business dey treat worker, customer and public well-well, e no be just profit or advertisement matter.

questions.q: A bank in Enugu sponsors free medical check-ups for residents of its host community every year, even though this is not required by any law. Which is the MAIN reason businesses undertake such social responsibility activities?
o: To build goodwill and trust with the host community
To reduce the amount of tax the company pays
To avoid paying workers their full wages
To eliminate rival businesses from the market
questions.e: Companies carry out voluntary community projects mainly to create a good image, earn public trust, and maintain a healthy relationship with the people around them, which can also boost long-term business success.
questions.p: Di main reason why company dey do free medical or community project na to build good name and trust with di people around dem, even though law no force dem.

questions.q: A textile factory in Kaduna pays all its statutory taxes promptly and provides steady employment for over 400 workers, yet it releases untreated dye chemicals into a stream used by nearby farmers for irrigation, damaging their crops. This situation best shows the company fulfilling its ___ responsibility while neglecting its ___ responsibility.
questions.e: Paying taxes and creating jobs are economic contributions to society, but harming farmers' livelihoods through pollution shows a failure in social responsibility, which is about caring for community welfare.
questions.p: Di factory dey pay tax and give people work, dat na economic responsibility, but e dey spoil farmers crop with waste, dat one na failure for social responsibility wey suppose protect community welfare.

questions.q: According to Carroll's pyramid of corporate social responsibility, which responsibility forms the FOUNDATION (base) that every business must first satisfy before pursuing the others?
questions.e: Carroll's pyramid places economic responsibility (being profitable and providing goods/services people need) as the base, because a business must first survive financially before it can obey laws, act ethically, or give to charity.
questions.p: For Carroll pyramid, economic responsibility (to make profit and provide goods/service) na di foundation, because business must first survive financially before e fit follow law, act ethical or do charity.
